observations: Screenshot-to-report mapping: 1.PNG = Executive Summary, 2.PNG = Executive Day Sheet, 3.PNG = Aging Report by Home Office, 4.PNG = Aging Report, 5.PNG = Income Allocation, 6.PNG = Allocation Detail, 7.PNG = Unallocated Payment/Adjustments, 8.PNG = Daily Journal Summary by Allocation, 9.PNG = WaterFall Report. Every report in the list has exactly one screenshot; none shows a popup, an expanded dropdown or a scrolled second view, so the contents of the Office, Office Group, Provider and Exclude Resp. Party Type SELECT dialogs and of the SEARCH lookups are not visible in this category. (The folder key is spelled 'montly'.) Title bar: 'Monthly Reports' at the left; 'PGID :2829 / OID :108' followed by a printer icon at the far right. Panel headers: 'SELECT REPORT' (left) and 'REPORT CRITERIA' (right). A splitter / collapse handle (three vertical dots) sits on the border between the two panels. SELECT REPORT is a single column of 9 radio items (no second column) with a large empty area below the last one, so the list is not clipped or scrollable; the list text is pixel-identical in all 9 screenshots. Global actions are the same on every report: CLEAR CRITERIA (slate-grey button with a refresh icon at the right end of the REPORT CRITERIA header bar), PRINT / PREVIEW (blue, printer icon) and ADD TO MY FAVORITES (blue, plus icon) in a footer bar at the bottom right of the criteria panel. Captured at 75% browser zoom. Footer, visible only in 5.PNG: '© 2026 Planet DDS | Privacy Policy | Page Time Left (hh:mm:ss) 1:58:18' ('Privacy Policy' is a blue link), a red italic notice 'Your browser zoom is set to 75%. This screen is best viewed, if zoom is set to 100%.' and a browser status-bar URL 'https://a1.denticon.com/ASCX/#'. 6.PNG and 9.PNG include a 1-3 px blue strip above the title bar (capture offset only). Header glyph caveat: at this capture size the section-header typeface renders capital G almost like C, so the pixels look like 'OFFICE/CROUP', 'DATE RANCE', 'CROUP BY', 'ACINC BY', 'ACINC' and 'RESPONSIBLE PARTY NAME RANCE'. They are transcribed as OFFICE/GROUP, DATE RANGE, GROUP BY, AGING BY, AGING and RESPONSIBLE PARTY NAME RANGE: each of these glyphs carries a one-pixel spur at the lower right that the true C's (in OFFICE, CREDIT, BALANCES) do not have, and the same letter is an unambiguous G in 'GROUP BY PROVIDER', 'Office Group' and 'Aging Report'. Defaults: every date field shows 11/21/2026 (the capture date), the unlabelled office box shows 108 (= OID in the title bar), Provider shows ALL, Exclude Resp. Party Type shows None. Read-only picker boxes (108, ALL, None) have a darker grey fill than editable inputs (dates, Start Name / End Name, Account Balance Over). Disabled controls (confirmed by colour sampling on all nine screenshots): 'Page Break' on Executive Summary; the 'Preferred Provider / Transaction Provider' radios and the Provider SELECT button on both aging reports. Nothing else is greyed out. Recurring patterns: OFFICE/GROUP (Office / Office Group radios plus the unlabelled 108 box with SELECT) appears on all 9 reports; PRINT FORMAT (PDF / Excel, default PDF) only on Executive Day Sheet, both aging reports, Daily Journal Summary by Allocation and WaterFall Report; REPORT FORMAT (Detail / Summary, default Detail) only on both aging reports, Income Allocation and Daily Journal Summary by Allocation; a Provider picker (default ALL) on Executive Summary, Income Allocation, Allocation Detail and both aging reports; seven reports use DATE RANGE with Start Date and End Date, while the two aging reports use a single Report Date. Only real uncertainty: 'Aging Report by Home Office' (3.PNG) and 'Aging Report' (4.PNG) have pixel-identical criteria panels whose last section, SORT BY, is cut off by the action bar with no scrollbar drawn - only the top 2 pixel rows of its two radio labels show. They are given as best readings with [?] ('Resp. Party Last name', 'Resp. Party ID'; see the control notes for the pixel evidence) and both reports are flagged possibly_truncated because further SORT BY rows or sections may exist below the cut.
